newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: South American port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: South American port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ARGENTINA, April 22 - Santa Fe - No vessels berthed, none in roads, none due. Max. recommended draft 23 ft. 4 ins. at access channel. Diamante - No vessels berthed, none in roads, 1 due. Max. recommended draft 23 ft. 4 ins. at passage KM 520. San Lorenzo - Seven vessels berthed of which 6 loading (1 soya, 4 maize, 1 sun oil). 1 Discharging chemical products. 8 Vessels in roads, 21 vessels due at 6 terminals this week and next. Forecast indicates that draft will fall approx. 0.20 m during next week. Pasa berth draft - 21 ft. 5 ins. Fw.

Rosario - Six vessels berthed of which 5 loading (4 maize, 1 soya), 1 awaiting orders. 6 Vessels in roads, 22 due within this week and next. Forecast indicates that draft will fall approx. 0.20 m during next week. Villa Constitucion - Two vessels berthed of which 1 loading maize, 1 discharging iron ore. No vessels in roads, 2 due. Elevator berths - Max. draft 22 ft. 0 ins. Fw. San Nicolas - Three vessels berthed of which 2 discharging (1 coal, 1 zinc), 1 loading zinc. 3 Vessels in roads, 6 due within the next week. Forecast indicates that draft will fall approx. 0.20 m during next week.

San Pedro - No vessels berthed, none in roads, 1 due. Forecast indicates that draft will fall approx. 0.20 m during next week. Max. drafts - the following max. Sailing drafts from up river ports (except Santa Fe and Diamante) are a result of new soundings carried out and an advanced dropping of Parana river levels - San Lorenzo/Rosario ports - 32 ft. 08 ins., San Nicolas/San Pedro - 33 ft. 00 ins. Fw. The draft is expected to fall further over the next month to 29 ft. 00 ins./30 ft. 00 ins. Buenos Aires - 16 vessels in port, 20 due within the next week. Max. recommended draft 31 ft. 6 ins. Fw. high tide Naabsa (guided by entrance channel). Dock sud max. draft 28/29 ft. Fw high tide Naabsa (guided by entrance channel).

Necochea - Four vessels berthed, all loading, of which 1 wheat, 2 maize, 1 sfmp. 5 Vessels in roads, 11 due within the next week. Max. recommended draft at entrance channel 40 ft. 0 ins. Bahia Blanca - Five vessels berthed, all loading, of which 1 maize, 1 wheat, 1 naphtha, 1 sfo, 1 fertiliser. No vessels in roads, 13 due within the next week. Drafts vary for individual berths.

BRAZIL, April 22 - Vitoria - Five vessels berthed of which 1 general cargo/container discharger/loader, 1 iron discharger, 1 vehicles/containers loader/discharger, 1 wheat discharger, 1 cellulose loader. Tubarao - 3 Iron ore loaders, 1 petroleum discharger. Praia Mole - 3 Steel products loaders. Portocel - 1 Cellulose vessel. Ubu - 1 Iron ore loader, 23 vessels waiting in roads.

Santos - 23 Vessels berthed of which 3 full containers loader/dischargers, 1 bulk cement, 3 container dischargers, 2 wheat dischargers, 6 general cargo/container loaders/dischargers, 1 general cargo loader, 1 bulk soya loader, 2 fertiliser dischargers, 1 chemical products loader, 1 chemical products discharger, 2 chemical products loaders/dischargers. 14 Vessels waiting in roads, 74 due over the next 7 days. Private terminals - Cosipa - 1 Bulk coal discharger, 1 iron ore discharger, 2 bulk steel products loaders. Ultrafertil - No vessels.

Paranagua - 11 Vessels berthed of which 1 fertiliser discharger, 1 container discharger, 2 general cargo dischargers, 2 pellets loaders, 2 general cargo loaders, 3 soya loaders. 27 Vessels waiting in roads of which 22 to load (10 soya, 12 pellets). 5 To discharge (2 fertiliser, 1 general cargo, 2 containers). 20 Vessels due over the next 7 days. Rio Grande - Seven vessels berthed of which 1 full container loader, 1 soya bean loader, 1 cellulose loader, 1 general cargo loader, 1 fertiliser loader, 2 expellers loaders. 2 Vessels waiting in roads, 13 due over the next 10 days.

Rio de Janeiro - Eight vessels berthed of which 1 general cargo/bulker discharger, 1 wheat discharger, 1 cotton discharger, 1 oil discharger, 3 steel products/general cargo dischargers, 1 steel products loader. Tecon - 3 Vessels, 27 due over the next 7 days.

CHILE, April 21 - Arica - Two vessels berthed, 4 berths vacant, 10 vessels due during the week. Iquique - Three vessels berthed and operating, 3 berths vacant, 14 vessels due this week. Antofagasta - Three vessels berthed, 4 berths vacant, 9 vessels due during week to load/discharge concentrates, bulk copper, containers and general cargo. Valparaiso - Six vessels berthed and operating, 1 berth vacant. 1 Berth (pier 2) out of service until April '98 for enlargement. 12 Vessels due during week, with 1 day delay expected. San Antonio - Six vessels in port operating, 5 berths vacant, 15 vessels due during week. Port busy but no waiting time.

Puerto Montt - Three vessels and 1 passenger vessel in port, 4 due during week. Punta Arenas - No vessels berthed, 7 due during week. Conception Bay ports - 14 Vessels due this week at different terminals. Talcahuano - No vessels berthed, 3 due this week, none in roads. San Vicente - Two vessels berthed and operating, 1 berth vacant, 6 vessels due during week. 1 Day berthing delay expected. Navy pier (Molo 500) - 1 Vessel berthed, none due during week. Steel pier - 1 Vessel berthed, none due during week. Coronel pier - 1 Vessel berthed. Oil terminal - 1 Berthed, none due during week. Lirquen - Two vessels berthed, 3 berths vacant, 5 vessels due in week. Penco - No vessels berthed.

PERU, April 21 - No strikes at any port. Callao - Four vessels anchored, 5 general cargo/container vessels berthed, no berthing delays. Paita - No vessels anchored, 1 fish meal/general cargo vessel berthed, no berthing delays. Bayovar, Pisco - No vessels, no delays. Talara - One vessel anchored, 1 oil tanker berthed, 7 days berthing delay expected. Chimbote - One fish meal vessel anchored. No vessels berthed, no berthing delays. Ilo - Two fish meal vessels anchored. No vessels berthed, No berthing delays.

VENEZUELA, April 21 - Puerto Cabello - Three vessels anchored, 12 berthed of which 5 grain cargo, 3 general cargo, 2 bulk cargo, 1 ro-ro, 1 containers. Piers 1 and 2 closed. Guanta - Three vessels anchored, 2 general cargo vessels berthed. April 22 - All ports working normally. Orinoco river - Draft as at 22/4, 31 ft. 6 ins. Puerto Ordaz - Three vessels operating of which 1 discharging manganese ore. 2 Loading (1 iron ore, 1 ferro manganese). 2 Vessels due. Mile 178 - Two vessels waiting at anchorage to load. Boca Grande - One vessel loading iron ore. Matanzas - Three vessels waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 6 operating of which 1 discharging general cargo, 5 loading steel products. 2 Vessels due.

Interalumina - One vessel loading aluminium. Venalum - One vessel loading aluminium, 1 due. Alcasa - One vessel discharging limestone, 1 due. Punta Cuchillo - One vessel loading refined products, 1 due. La Guaira - Eight vessels due, 3 under repair. Puerto Cabello - Two vessels waiting at anchorage, 17 operating of which 16 loading/discharging general cargo, 1 discharging soya beans. 11 Vessels due. Guanta - One vessel discharging wheat, 5 due. Amuay - Two vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 3 loading refined products. Cardon - Two vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 4 loading refined products. Guaranao - One vessel discharging wood-pulp.

Maracaibo - Two vessels loading/discharging general cargo. Puerto Miranda - Three vessels loading crude oil. El Tablazo - One vessel loading urea. Buoy B. 71 - One vessel loading coal. La Salina - Three vessels loading crude oil. Bajo Grande - Refined products terminal - 2 Vessels loading refined products. Sanfrancisco - One vessel loading crude oil. La Ceiba - One vessel loading coal. Punta Palma, Punta Camacho, San Lorenzo - No vessels.
